answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can mandate verifiable delay functions. Each node must solve a sequential cryptographic puzzle across a designated time delta, preventing parallel precomputation. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce single-threaded execution time per identity and cannot simply echo stale proofs across a tiered lotus network. However, attackers wielding custom ASICs evaluate puzzles faster, creating an unfair throughput advantage.
